Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 6.pdf ---
SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming online

during the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page. Quality and traceability of the data matter a lot too, since the whole point is feeding
trustworthy numbers into the international climate change conversation, so whatever
comes out the other end needs solid metadata and documentation attached, not just raw
numbers.

Sistema: SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)

Resumo executivo: The SLCCI system shall operationalize the production, validation, cross-calibration, distribution and long-term preservation of satellite altimetry data for sea-level climate research. It shall transform more than thirty years of Earth observation archives into traceable, documented per-mission and merged gridded climate products, supporting reprocessing as algorithms, calibration methods and satellite missions evolve.

Escopo: The system shall operationally process multi-mission satellite altimetry data into validated, calibrated and archived sea-level climate products.
  Em escopo: Ingestion of altimetry data from multiple satellite missions
  Em escopo: Calibration and validation processing
  Em escopo: Cross-calibration between satellite missions
  Em escopo: Generation of per-mission measurement-track products
  Em escopo: Generation of merged gridded sea-level products
  Em escopo: Archiving of baseline, intermediate and final data
  Em escopo: Historical reprocessing with updated algorithms and calibration methods
  Em escopo: Product cataloguing, metadata and documentation management
  Em escopo: Operational monitoring and user-request handling
  Fora de escopo: Near-real-time delivery — the project is limited to delayed-time and reprocessed historical climate data
  Fora de escopo: Operational ocean forecasting services — these belong to separate oceanographic services
  Fora de escopo: Formal IT service-management and incident-ticketing frameworks — explicitly excluded from the project
  Fora de escopo: General-public and commercial-customer services — the target audience is the specialized climate research community
  Premissa: PA-01: Existing prototype algorithms and production procedures are available for operationalization.
  Premissa: PA-02: Relevant satellite altimetry data can be accessed from the participating missions or their repositories.
  Premissa: PA-03: [INFERIDO] Climate researchers have access to a network connection and can use documented scientific data formats.
  Premissa: PA-04: Existing ocean-data infrastructure can be reused where technically appropriate.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Operational scope): The system shall support delayed-time and historical reprocessing, not near-real-time delivery.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Sustainability): The operational solution shall be sustainable for long-term operation within the available cost constraints.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Evolution): The solution shall accommodate new satellite missions and replaceable processing algorithms.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Reuse): Existing proven ocean-data infrastructure shall be reused where appropriate.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Production Operations Team (Usuário primário): Run, schedule, monitor and control operational data-production workflows.
  STK-02 - Scientific Validation Team (Usuário secundário): Perform scientific validation, investigate anomalies and support new-product definition.
  STK-03 - Product Quality Approvers (Usuário secundário): Review and approve product quality before publication.
  STK-04 - Catalog and Metadata Team (Usuário primário): Maintain catalog entries, metadata and product documentation.
  STK-05 - Operations Support Team (Usuário primário): Monitor operational status, handle incidents and respond to user requests.
  STK-06 - Climate Research Community (Usuário primário): Discover, access and trust documented sea-level climate products for climate modelling and research.
  STK-07 - ESA Climate Change Initiative (Stakeholder externo): Obtain an operational sea-level climate-data capability aligned with the broader initiative.
  STK-08 - Satellite Mission Data Providers (Stakeholder externo): Provide mission altimetry data and associated source information for processing.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Finalidade climática: Sea-level data shall be produced for delayed-time climate research and historical climate records.
  RN-002 - Produtos obrigatórios: The initiative shall provide both per-mission measurement-track products and merged gridded products.
  RN-003 - Consistência entre missões: Measurements from different satellite missions shall be cross-calibrated to form a consistent climate record.
  RN-004 - Preservação da linhagem de dados: Baseline data and intermediate processing data shall be preserved for future reprocessing and traceability.
  RN-005 - Aprovação da qualidade: Products shall be made available for research use only after quality assessment and approval by the designated quality authority.
  RN-006 - Documentação e metadados: Each published product shall include sufficient metadata and documentation to support interpretation and scientific reuse.
  RN-007 - Evolução científica: Processing methods shall be replaceable when algorithms or calibration methods improve.
  RN-008 - Integração de novas missões: New satellite missions shall be incorporable during the project lifecycle.

Glossário:
  Altimetry: Satellite-based measurement technique used to derive ocean surface height.
  Per-mission measurement-track product: A product containing processed sea-level measurements associated with one satellite mission and its measurement tracks.
  Merged gridded product: A spatially gridded product combining cross-calibrated measurements from multiple satellite missions.
  Cross-calibration: Process of adjusting measurements from different missions to improve consistency across the combined climate record.
  Delayed-time: Data-delivery mode in which measurements are processed after acquisition rather than being provided in near-real time.
  Reprocessing: Repeated processing of historical data using updated algorithms, calibration methods or configurations.
  Baseline data: Original or reference datasets preserved as inputs for processing and future reprocessing.
  Intermediate data: Data generated between ingestion and final-product production and retained for traceability and reprocessing.
  Processing algorithm version: A uniquely identified version of the scientific logic used to transform input data into products.
  Product lineage: Traceable relationship between a product, its source datasets, processing steps, configurations and approvals.
  NRT: Near-real-time data delivery, explicitly outside the SLCCI scope.

archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming onlineduring the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank

Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

Rastrear os Requisitos PE (5.1)
Propósito
O objetivo de Rastrear os Requisitos é garantir que os requisitos e designs em 
diferentes níveis estejam alinhados entre si e gerenciar os efeitos da 
mudança em um nível nos requisitos relacionados.
Descrição
Rastrear os Requisitos: analisa e mantém os relacionamentos entre 
requisitos, designs, componentes de solução e outros produtos de trabalho 
para análise de impacto, cobertura e alocação.
Entradas
• Requisitos: podem ser rastreados para outros requisitos (incluindo 
metas, objetivos, requisitos de negócio, requisitos de stakeholder, 
requisitos de solução e requisitos de transição), componentes de 
solução, recursos visuais, regras de negócio e outros produtos de 
trabalho.
• Designs: podem ser rastreados para outros requisitos, componentes de 
solução e outros produtos de trabalho.
Saídas 
• Requisitos (rastreados): têm relações claramente definidas com outros 
requisitos, componentes de solução ou versões, fases ou iterações, 
dentro de um escopo de solução, de modo que a cobertura e os efeitos da 
mudança sejam claramente identificáveis.
• Designs (rastreados): relacionamentos claramente definidos com outros 
requisitos, componentes da solução ou versões, fases ou iterações, 
dentro de um escopo de solução, de modo que a cobertura e os efeitos da 
alteração sejam claramente identificáveis.
Manter os Requisitos PE (5.2)
Propósito
A finalidade de Manter os Requisitos é manter a precisão e a consistência dos 
requisitos ao longo e além da alteração durante todo o ciclo de vida de 
requisitos e apoiar a reutilização de requisitos em outras soluções.

If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.
Perhaps your current system is a shapeless mass of history and mystery like the one in Figure 21-2. 
Imagine that you’ve been asked to implement some new functionality in region A in this figure. 
Begin by recording the new requirements in a structured SRS or in a requirements management tool. 
When you add the new functionality, you’ll have to figure out how it interfaces to or fits in with the 
existing system. The bridges in Figure 21-2 between region A and your current system represent these 
interfaces. This analysis provides insight into the white portion of the current system, region B. In 
addition to the requirements for region A, this insight is the new knowledge you need to capture.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 399
FIGURE 21-2 Adding enhancement A to an ill-documented existing system provides some visibility into the 
B area.
Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- The system is part of ESA's Climate Change Initiative (CCI), one of about eleven parallel projects each covering a different climate variable.
- The system must take an existing science prototype/production setup and turn it into an operational, day-to-day system.
- The system ingests altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
- The system performs calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions.
- The system produces two product types: a per-mission along-track product and a merged multi-mission gridded product.
- The system must include an archive to preserve baseline and intermediate data, since reprocessing will happen repeatedly.
- Internal users include scientists (deeper validation/product definition), quality reviewers who sign off on products, catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests).
- External users are the climate research community, not the general public or commercial customers.
- Near-real-time (NRT) delivery is explicitly out of scope; the system is delayed-time / reprocessed-data only.
- Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (e.g. ITIL-style) are explicitly out of scope.
- The system must be cost-sustainable to operate long-term, not just a one-off build.
- The system must be flexible enough to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time.
- The system should reuse existing proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
- Output data must include solid metadata and documentation to ensure quality and traceability.

em_escopo: Ingesting altimetry data from multiple satellite missions
Calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions
Generating the merged multi-mission gridded product
Archiving baseline and intermediate data to support repeated reprocessing
Workflows for scientists (deeper validation / product definition), quality reviewers (sign-off), catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests)
Making data available to the climate research community (external users)
Metadata and documentation attached to each output product
Ability to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time
fora_de_escopo: Near-real-time (NRT) delivery — the system is exclusively for reprocessed/delayed-time data
Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (ITIL-style)
Serving the general public or commercial customers — the target audience is only the climate research community
premissas: PA-01: [INFERRED] Proven infrastructure already exists for broader ocean data that can be reused.
PA-02: The science (algorithms, validation, prototyping) has already been developed by another team; the project starts from an existing prototype, not from scratch.
restricoes: REST-01 (Financial): The system must be financially sustainable for long-term operation, not just a one-off build.
REST-02 (Technological): The system should, wherever it makes sense, reuse already-proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
REST-03 (Organizational): The system is part of a larger ESA effort (Climate Change Initiative), with about eleven parallel projects covering different climate variables.

stakeholders.descricao: Scientists — brought in for deeper validation or definition of new products.
Quality reviewers — evaluate and sign off on generated products before release.
Catalog/metadata staff — maintain the product catalog and metadata.
Operational staff — monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests.
Climate research community (external users) — researchers doing climate modelling who need reliable, well-documented sea level data.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The system is one of about eleven parallel ESA Climate Change Initiative projects, each covering a different climate variable — this project covers sea level.
Products must go through calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions before being considered consistent.
Reprocessing happens repeatedly as algorithms and calibration methods evolve, so baseline and intermediate data must never be lost.
The target audience is exclusively the climate research community — not the general public or commercial customers.
Near-real-time (NRT) delivery use cases are explicitly excluded — the system only serves the reprocessed/delayed-time data flow.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must ingest altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
The system must perform calibration and validation of ingested altimetry data.
The system must perform cross-calibration between different satellite missions to ensure consistency.
The system must generate the per-mission along-track product.
The system must generate the merged multi-mission gridded product, blending data from multiple missions into a single climate record.
The system must archive baseline and intermediate data to support future reprocessing without loss.
The system must allow scientists to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed.
The system must allow quality reviewers to evaluate and sign off on products before release.
The system must maintain a catalog with metadata for generated products.
The system must allow operational staff to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests.
The system must attach metadata and documentation to output data, ensuring quality and traceability.
The system must support onboarding new satellite missions over time.
The system must support swapping in updated processing algorithms without interrupting existing operations.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must be flexible enough to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over the life of the project, without requiring a full rebuild.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a scientist, I want to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed, so that scientific quality is maintained as the system evolves.
As a quality reviewer, I want to evaluate and approve products, so that only validated data is released.
As a member of the catalog/metadata team, I want to maintain the product catalog and metadata, so that the data stays discoverable and well-documented.
As a member of the operational staff, I want to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests, so that day-to-day operations keep running.
As a climate research community member, I want to access reliable, well-documented sea level data, so that I can trust it and build my research on it.

As a system operator, I want to reprocess historical data when algorithms or calibration methods improve, without losing baseline or intermediate data, so that the climate record stays accurate over time.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Process satellite altimetry data — the system ingests data from multiple missions, calibrates and validates it, cross-calibrates between missions, and generates the per-mission and multi-mission gridded products.
Review and release product — a quality reviewer evaluates a newly generated product and approves it for release, or flags it for correction.
Reprocess historical data — an operator triggers reprocessing of archived baseline/intermediate data using an updated algorithm or calibration method, without losing prior data.
Onboard new satellite mission — an operator or scientist configures the system to ingest data from a newly available satellite mission.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given altimetry data from two or more satellite missions, when cross-calibration is performed, then the resulting measurements are consistent across missions.
Given a reprocessing run using an updated algorithm, when processing completes, then the baseline and intermediate data from previous runs remain intact and accessible.
Given a newly generated product, when a quality reviewer evaluates it, then the product is approved for release or flagged for correction.
Given a released dataset, when a climate research community member accesses it, then the dataset includes metadata and documentation sufficient to trace its origin and processing history.
Given a new satellite mission becomes available, when it is onboarded, then that mission's data is processed without requiring a rebuild of the existing processing pipelines.
